lists.name: Grade 3 — Plants, Animals and Our Earth
lists.description: Life- and earth-science words 8–9 year olds read in science units: plant parts, animal groups, volcanoes and how living things survive.
lists.subject: science

words.definition: A tiny animal with six legs and a body in three parts
words.example: A ladybug is an insect with red wings and black spots.

words.definition: The dark, loose dirt that plants grow in
words.example: We pressed the bean seeds into the wet soil.

words.definition: The part of a plant that grows underground and drinks up water
words.example: The carrot is the root of the plant, so we eat it.

words.definition: The small part of a plant that a new plant grows from
words.example: Mia planted a sunflower seed in a paper cup.

words.definition: Low land between hills or mountains, often with a river
words.example: Our bus drove down into a green valley full of farms.

words.definition: A warm-blooded animal with hair that feeds its babies milk
words.example: A whale lives in the sea, but it is a mammal, not a fish.

words.definition: A cold-blooded animal with dry, scaly skin, like a snake or lizard
words.example: The turtle is a reptile that can hide inside its shell.

words.definition: Rock holding the shape of a plant or animal from long ago
words.example: Ben found a fossil of a tiny shell at the beach.

words.definition: A mountain that can blow out hot melted rock, ash and smoke
words.example: The volcano rumbled, and red lava poured down its side.

words.definition: To pick and gather crops when they are ready to eat
words.example: In the fall, farmers harvest pumpkins from the fields.

words.definition: Yellow dust in flowers that bees carry from plant to plant
words.example: The bee's fuzzy legs were covered in pollen.

words.definition: To stay alive, even when things are hard or dangerous
words.example: Camels can survive many days in the desert without water.

words.definition: To turn used things like cans and paper into something new
words.example: We recycle our milk jugs so they can become new bottles.

words.definition: The power that makes things move, grow, light up or warm up
words.example: Plants get energy from sunlight to help them grow.

words.definition: A piece of land with water all around it
words.example: We took a boat to a small island in the middle of the lake.

words.definition: An animal that hunts and eats other animals
words.example: The owl is a predator that hunts mice at night.

words.definition: No longer living anywhere on Earth
words.example: Dinosaurs became extinct millions of years ago.

words.definition: To change over time to fit a new place
words.example: Animals adapt to cold places by growing thick fur.

words.definition: The slow wearing away of land by water, wind or ice
words.example: Waves cause erosion that slowly eats away the cliff.

lists.name: Grade 3 — Communities and Places
lists.description: Social-studies words for 3rd graders: who lives where, the places a town shares and the people who keep it running.
lists.subject: geography

words.definition: A small group of houses and shops, smaller than a town
words.example: Everyone in the village came to the summer fair.

words.definition: A very large, busy town where many people live and work
words.example: The city has tall buildings, busy streets and a big zoo.

words.definition: A drawing that shows where places, roads and rivers are
words.example: We used a map to find the way to the park.

words.definition: A place where people buy and sell food and other goods
words.example: Grandma buys fresh peaches at the market every Saturday.

words.definition: A person who lives next door or close to you
words.example: Our neighbor waters our plants when we go away.

words.definition: A road or path built over a river, road or valley
words.example: We walked across the bridge and watched the boats below.

words.definition: People who live in the same area and help each other
words.example: Our community planted trees along Main Street.

words.definition: A building where you can borrow books for free
words.example: I took home three books about dragons from the library.

words.definition: A building where people look at art or old, special things
words.example: At the museum we saw a giant dinosaur skeleton.

words.definition: The leader chosen to run a town or city
words.example: The mayor cut the ribbon to open the new playground.

words.definition: A land with its own people, leaders and flag
words.example: Canada is a big country with lots of lakes and forests.

words.definition: A building where workers and machines make things
words.example: The chocolate factory makes thousands of candy bars a day.

words.definition: A person who helps without getting paid for it
words.example: Dad is a volunteer who reads stories at the hospital.

words.definition: One of the seven giant areas of land on Earth
words.example: Africa is the continent where wild lions and giraffes live.

words.definition: The number of people who live in a place
words.example: Our town's population grew when the new houses were built.

words.definition: Something a family or group has done the same way for years
words.example: Making pancakes on Sunday is a tradition in our house.

words.definition: In the countryside, with farms and open land, far from cities
words.example: My cousin lives in a rural area with cows and corn fields.

words.definition: In a city, with lots of buildings and people close together
words.example: Urban parks give city kids a place to run and play.

words.definition: A family member who lived a long, long time ago
words.example: My ancestor sailed across the ocean over a hundred years ago.

lists.name: Grade 3 — Words for Thinking and Learning
lists.description: The words 3rd graders hear in every lesson and see on worksheets: observe, explain, solve, revise and more.
lists.subject: english

words.definition: A thought or plan that comes into your mind
words.example: Lily had a great idea for our class art project.

words.definition: Something you ask when you want to know or find out
words.example: Raise your hand if you have a question about the story.

words.definition: What you say or write back when someone asks you something
words.example: Write your answer in the box below the math problem.

words.definition: To pick one thing from a group of things
words.example: You may choose a red, blue or green folder.

words.definition: To see or hear something and pay attention to it
words.example: Did you notice the bird's nest in the tree?

words.definition: To keep something in your mind or bring it back later
words.example: Remember to bring your library book back tomorrow.

words.definition: To tell about something clearly so others understand it
words.example: Can you explain how you got the answer?

words.definition: To make a picture of something in your mind
words.example: Imagine you could fly over your school like a bird.

words.definition: To watch something carefully to learn about it
words.example: We observe the caterpillar every day to see how it changes.

words.definition: To do something again and again to get better at it
words.example: I practice my spelling words before every test.

words.definition: Something hard or wrong that needs to be worked out or fixed
words.example: Our problem was that the boat kept sinking, so we added foam.

words.definition: A small fact or piece of information about something
words.example: Add one more detail about how the dragon looked.

words.definition: To find the answer or the way to fix something
words.example: It took us ten minutes to solve the riddle.

words.definition: To make up your mind and choose what to do
words.example: We could not decide whether to play tag or soccer.

words.definition: What a story, talk or piece of writing is mostly about
words.example: The topic of my report is sea turtles.

words.definition: To look for facts in books or online to learn about something
words.example: We will research penguins and share three facts with the class.

words.definition: To put things neatly in order so they are easy to find
words.example: Let's organize the crayons by color.

words.definition: A group of sentences about one main idea
words.example: Start a new paragraph when you write about the next day.

words.definition: To change your writing to make it clearer or better
words.example: After reading it aloud, I decided to revise my ending.
